You seem to be asking two different questions. One is why they require registration. The second is why registration must state a party.

For the first it is a matter of insuring only valid citizens qualified to vote can and do vote. Since voting is anonymous, there is no way of removing a vote if you determine someone not eligible did vote. You could be a noncitizen, you could be a convicted felon who hasn't regained the franchise, you could be voting for someone else who hasn't shown up yet.

As for party registration. I have never lived anywhere that required party registration. I'm not even sure there are any. It would kind of surprise me. However, parties are private clubs. You can only make decisions for a party if you are a member (assuming you do not live in an open primary state -- the Constitutionality of which has always struck me as suspect). So if you want to vote in primaries, and not just general elections, you need to register for the party in which you want a say.

I don't understand why its important I choose a party when I register to vote. It seems as if its a way to single yourself out.

You need to register in order to help support the case that you are a citizen who lives at the location you claim, and not some other district. Otherwise people just might drive all over the place and to different states on election day casting votes.

As far as choosing the party you prefer, that is option. You don't have to choose a party to vote for president. However, if you wish to vote in any of the primaries, many states & parties require you to declare that party in advance. These are private elections of the Democrat or Republican party piggy backing on our government election system. In some states you don't have to declare party affiliation until you walk in and request a ballot for democratic primaries or republican primaries.
Voters are registered to prove they are a citizen who is entitled to vote and you can register as an independent with no party affiliation.
